v1.body: This app links to your WhatsApp as a companion device using an unofficial component. WhatsApp may not permit this; use it at your own risk. Nothing is sent without your approval.
v1.title: WhatsApp terms
Use your Claude subscription?
v1.body: The app runs the Claude Code you installed, under your own sign-in, to analyse chats.
v1.sent: The text of the chat being analysed; transcripts of its voice notes; pictures in it when "Read pictures with Anthropic" is on; older messages of this chat, or of all chats if you chose that.
v1.never: Names, phone numbers, your other chats (unless you chose "all my chats"), your calendar event titles.
v1.who: Anthropic processes the text under its consumer terms.
v1.goodToKnow: Runs the Claude Code you installed, under your own sign-in; Anthropic processes the text under its consumer terms. Anthropic changed its subscription rules several times in 2026 - if it changes again, the app shows a sign-in error and chats wait. Runs count against your 5-hour and weekly usage. Paid extra usage is off unless you turn it on.

v1.title: Use your Gemini subscription (experimental)?
v1.body: The app runs the unmodified Antigravity CLI you installed, under your own sign-in, to analyse chats.
v1.sent: The text of the chat being analysed; transcripts of its voice notes; the last {{days}} days of this chat; never pictures.
v1.never: Names, phone numbers, your other chats (unless you chose "all my chats"), your calendar event titles.
v1.who: Google processes it under the Antigravity terms.
v1.goodToKnow: Google's terms for Antigravity forbid using it with "third-party software, tools, or services", and Google has suspended accounts for it; Google staff have also said that running the official CLI on your own computer is fine. The app runs the unmodified Antigravity CLI with your own sign-in and nothing else - the risk to your account is yours. Antigravity keeps a copy of every request on this computer. Google's supported way is Gemini with an API key (under Advanced). Terms read on <bdi>2026-09-28</bdi>.
v1.accept: I accept the risk - use Gemini

intro.body1: The agent creates events in your own calendar. For that it needs a free key that belongs to you.
intro.body2: Five short steps on Google's site, about five minutes. You can also do this later.
intro.privacy: The agent reads the busy and free times of your calendar and creates only the events you approved.

step1.i1: Open the Google Cloud console and create a new project. Any name will do.
step1.i2: With that project selected, open the Google Calendar API page and press Enable.
step1.tip: If a page asks you to choose an organisation, choose No organisation.
step1.title: Create a project

step2.i1: Open the OAuth consent screen and choose External.
step2.i2: Fill in an app name and your own email address, then save.
step2.i3: On the Audience page press Publish app, so that the sign-in does not expire after seven days.
step2.testingBody: In Testing mode Google signs you out after seven days, and the agent asks you to connect again.
step2.testingTitle: What happens if I leave it in Testing?
step2.title: Set up the consent screen

step3.i1: Open Credentials, press Create credentials, then OAuth client ID.
step3.i2: For Application type choose Desktop app - not Web application.
step3.i3: Use the name below, so you recognise it later.
step3.title: Create the key

step4.drop: Drop the JSON file you downloaded here
step4.hint: The file stays where it is - only its contents are read.
step4.title: Add the key file

step5.firewall: Windows may ask whether this app can use the network - Cancel or Allow both work.
step5.title: Sign in
step5.unverified: Google will say it has not verified this app. That is expected: the app is yours and you are its only user. Choose Advanced, then Go to (your app name).

agy.disclosure: Google's terms for Antigravity forbid using it with "third-party software, tools, or services", and Google has suspended accounts for it; Google staff have also said that running the official CLI on your own computer is fine. The app runs the unmodified Antigravity CLI with your own sign-in and nothing else - the risk to your account is yours. Antigravity keeps a copy of every request on this computer. Google's supported way is Gemini with an API key (under Advanced). Terms read on <bdi>{{termsDate}}</bdi>.
